name: Stoutmantle's Response to Solomon
summary: From Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle sends word to Lakeshire that no soldiers can be spared for Redridge Mountains.

sections.title: A Plea Denied
sections.body: Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire asks Sentinel Hill for help as Blackrock orcs and gnolls press his town. Gryan Stoutmantle answers in writing and mourns Lakeshire's losses. Yet Westfall faces a war of its own. The People's Militia formed after the Crown withdrew its garrison, and farmers and volunteers now fight the Defias Brotherhood alone. Stoutmantle's forces are already bleeding and stretched thin, with no men to spare for another abandoned frontier.

sections.title: The Kingdom's Neglect
sections.body: Redridge and Westfall share a grim plight. The royal court in Stormwind City has forsaken them both. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and the kingdom's standing army is mysteriously kept from provincial borders. Outlying towns must form volunteer watches or perish. Solomon receives the sealed reply and sees that neither town can save the other. The realm frays while the capital remains silent.

faq.q: What is written in Stoutmantle's response?
faq.answer: Gryan Stoutmantle writes that Westfall fights a brutal war against the Defias Brotherhood and has lost Stormwind's army, as Redridge has. He mourns the fallen defenders but declines Magistrate Solomon's request for reinforcements.

faq.q: Why did Solomon ask Westfall for help in the first place?
aliases: why did lakeshire ask for the militia
faq.answer: Lakeshire faces heavy assaults by gnolls and Blackrock orcs. Magistrate Solomon's plea to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind has brought no troops, so he asks the People's Militia across Elwynn for help from fellow frontier defenders.

faq.q: Why can't the People's Militia spare any troops?
faq.answer: The People's Militia is a volunteer army struggling to hold Sentinel Hill and the surrounding plains against the Defias Brotherhood. Casualties mount daily, and without regular army support, sending fighters to Lakeshire would leave Westfall undefended.

faq.q: Why isn't the Stormwind Army protecting these towns?
faq.answer: No one in either town knows why the Stormwind Army is absent. Stoutmantle writes that Stormwind withdrew its troops and left Westfall defenseless, while Solomon wonders what could call the army away from its people. Both regions rely on local volunteers.

angles.text: For the Alliance, this letter shows outlying settlements pleading with one another for aid while the capital withholds its forces.
As a human defender, you see Westfall and Redridge struggling to survive without Stormwind's royal guards.
